newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ Oil & Gas expands exploration programme.
newsitem.headline: NZ Oil & Gas expands exploration programme.

text.p: New Zealand Oil and Gas Ltd said on Thursday the group would significantly increase its exploration drilling activity during the next 12 months.
The group will participate in at least four wells in Western Australia through its 56 percent-owned subsidiary Pan Pacific Petroleum NL.

NZ Oil and Gas has farmed out 7.5 percent of its interest in offshore Carnarvon Basin permit WA-259-P where two wildcat exploration wells, Buck-1 and Bugle-1, are to be drilled in August and September 1997. The group had a 22.5 percent stake in the permit before the farm out to Petroz NL.
It said the operator, Apache Energy, estimated potential on the high side of up to 80 million barrels recoverable for Buck-1 and up to 60 million barrels recoverable for Bugle-1.
NZ Oil and Gas said its arrangement with Petroz would reduce its drilling costs by 50 percent and still leave it with a substantial interest in the project.

The group recently announced drilling would begin on its Chervil-6 appraisal well towards the end of June. It has a 23 percent interest in the well, which it said could result in increased oil recovery from the producing Chervil Field of 1.5 to six million barrels.

Drilling is scheduled to begin later this year on another offshore Canarvon basin well, Cadell-1, in the TP-7 permit. NZ Oil and Gas, which has a 4.1 percent stake, said the Cadell project held a potential of 30 million barrels of recoverable oil.

The company said it had extended the closing date for tenders in its "highly prospective" West Maui permit to early October, which would allow interested parties time to complete technical evaluations.
NZ Oil & Gas and Pan Pacific each own half the West Maui licence.
